nodes.name: Hourly Schedule
nodes.notes: Starts the workflow on a timer — every 12 h. No input data; downstream nodes fetch what they need.

nodes.name: Read Pending Queue (Google Sheets)
nodes.notes: Reads every row from 'Email Tracker' — the read side of the store, e.g. for a digest or a downstream sync. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Normalize Email Payload
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Normalize incoming email records to a stable schema Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Work in Batches
nodes.notes: Loop controller — releases 20 item(s) per pass. Output 2 (loop) processes the batch, output 1 (done) fires after the last batch. Watch out: Output 2 is the loop body, output 1 fires once after the last batch. Wiring these backwards is the classic mistake.

nodes.name: Process Batch Item
nodes.notes: POST https://api.example.com/v1/emails — retries 3× with backoff on failure. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: API key / bearer for the target API. Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.

nodes.name: Respect Rate Limits
nodes.notes: Pauses 2 seconds — spacing calls to respect rate limits. Watch out: Long waits survive restarts, but the resume URL is single-use.

nodes.name: Aggregate Batch Results
nodes.notes: Collapses all items into a single summary item (for counts and run stats).

nodes.name: Mark Completed in Airtable
nodes.notes: Upserts into Airtable's 'Emails' table, matched on messageId — safe to re-run without creating duplicates. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Airtable PAT. airtable.com/create/tokens → create a Personal Access Token.

nodes.name: Stamp Completion Time
nodes.notes: Stamps completedAt with the current time for auditing.

nodes.name: Persist Run Metadata
nodes.notes: Saves key fields onto the execution record — searchable later in n8n's execution list.

nodes.name: Fingerprint for Idempotency
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Build a stable idempotency key per email (djb2 hash, no deps) Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Drop Already-Processed Items
nodes.notes: Cross-execution dedupe: remembers keys it has processed before and drops repeats — the idempotency guard. Watch out: Cross-execution memory persists. After changing the key field, clear stored keys or old keys keep matching.

nodes.name: Serialize Run Output (CSV)
nodes.notes: Serializes items to a CSV binary file.

nodes.name: Archive Row Snapshot
nodes.notes: Appends a new row to 'Email Tracker' — a human-readable audit trail that doesn't require opening n8n to inspect. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Load Previous Snapshot
nodes.notes: Searches Airtable's 'Emails' table by formula (={LastModified} > DATEADD(NOW(), -1, 'days')) for records the pipeline hasn't handled yet. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Airtable PAT. airtable.com/create/tokens → create a Personal Access Token.

nodes.name: Compute Drift vs Snapshot
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Compare current metrics with the previous snapshot Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Summarize Run Stats
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes runAt, itemCount, status. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

nodes.name: Append Audit Row (Airtable)
nodes.notes: Creates a new record in Airtable's 'Emails' table. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Airtable PAT. airtable.com/create/tokens → create a Personal Access Token.

# Follow up: Google Sheets, Airtable & Slack

**Pattern:** Drip Sequence · **Level:** Expert · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers newsletters work end to end across Google Sheets, Airtable, Slack and Gmail.

It moves through 19 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. Hourly Schedule
2. Read Pending Queue (Google Sheets)
3. Normalize Email Payload
4. Work in Batches
5. Process Batch Item
6. Respect Rate Limits
7. Aggregate Batch Results
8. Mark Completed in Airtable
9. Stamp Completion Time
10. Persist Run Metadata
11. Fingerprint for Idempotency
12. Drop Already-Processed Items
13. Serialize Run Output (CSV)
14. Archive Row Snapshot
15. Load Previous Snapshot
16. Compute Drift vs Snapshot
17. Summarize Run Stats
18. Append Audit Row (Airtable)
19. Send Summary to Slack

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Gmail → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing newsletters work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Hourly Schedule → Read Pending Queue (Google Sheets) → Normalize Email Payload → Work in Batches → Process Batch Item → Respect Rate Limits → Aggregate Batch Results → Mark Completed in Airtable → Stamp Completion Time → Persist Run Metadata → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → Serialize Run Output (CSV) → Archive Row Snapshot → Load Previous Snapshot → Compute Drift vs Snapshot → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Airtable) → Send Summary to Slack → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Gmail → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Google Sheets and Airtable aligned by hand for newsletters
- Newsletters sequences that run over days and must survive a restart before Google Sheets
- A backlog too large to push into Google Sheets in one pass, across 22 nodes
- Newsletters work where "Read Pending Queue (Google Sheets)" is still a manual step before Google Sheets

## You get

- Keeps Google Sheets and Airtable in step for newsletters, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in Google Sheets or Airtable are skipped, across all 22 nodes of this newsletters build
- A failed Google Sheets or Airtable call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 22 nodes in this newsletters build
- The pause before Google Sheets is durable — a newsletters run survives a restart
- Batches the work so Google Sheets rate limits never break a newsletters run

## Before first run
Connect credentials: API key / bearer for the target API; Airtable PAT; Google OAuth2; Google OAuth2 / service account; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

The batch size and the Wait between iterations exist specifically to respect the downstream API's rate limit — processing everything as fast as possible just gets the workflow throttled or banned. Marking items completed only after a batch succeeds leaves a clean resume point if the run dies mid-way, instead of an ambiguous half-processed state.

## Practice exercises

Already production-grade — deepen your understanding:

1. Lower the batch size and raise the wait — measure the throughput/reliability tradeoff directly.
2. Simulate a failed item mid-batch and see exactly what 'Mark Completed' captures.
3. Point the queue read at a different store platform.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**API key / bearer for the target API**
Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.
_Gotcha:_ Store it as a credential, never typed into the node's parameters.

**Airtable PAT**
airtable.com/create/tokens → create a Personal Access Token.
_Gotcha:_ Scope the token to the specific base, and grant `data.records:write`. Field names are case-sensitive.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

**Google OAuth2**
Google Cloud Console → enable Gmail API → OAuth consent screen → OAuth client ID (Web).
_Gotcha:_ Add n8n's OAuth redirect URL exactly as shown in the credential, or the consent loop fails.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**HTTP node returns 401 or 403**
Cause: Wrong or unscoped credential, or the API expects a header this request isn't sending.
Fix: Verify the key directly with curl first, then confirm the auth type matches what the API documents.

**HTTP node returns 429**
Cause: Rate limited by the provider.
Fix: Raise the wait between calls or lower the batch size. Retries already back off, but they cannot beat a hard quota.

**The loop runs forever or exits immediately**
Cause: The loop output and the done output are wired the wrong way round.
Fix: Output 2 is the loop body; output 1 fires after the last batch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## ⏱ Rate limiting

Work is batched and spaced with Wait so provider quotas aren't tripped. If you hit 429s, lower the batch size or raise the wait — throughput drops, reliability rises.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your newsletters process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- Airtable: scope the PAT to this one base and to `data.records:write`; a token scoped to the workspace can rewrite every base.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.
- Gmail: request the narrowest send/read scope the nodes need — full mailbox access is rarely required.

The HTTP node sends a secret: keep it in a header credential, never in the URL — query strings land in proxy and execution logs.

**Do not log**
newsletters payloads carry personal data (names, email addresses, phone numbers). Log the record id and the outcome, not the record. n8n retains full execution data by default — turn that down for this workflow in Settings → Executions if these runs touch real contacts.
